name: Lupine Science
mission: Make AI predictions of new materials checkable before a lab commits to them.
oneLiner: Lupine Science measures where machine-learned models of atoms go wrong, against published references and pass/fail gates set in advance, and publishes every verdict, failures included.
description: Lupine Science is an early-stage, founder-led research company. We independently measure the errors of machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs), test corrections against preregistered gates, record any amendment made after results are seen, and publish the verdict: pass, fail or abstain. Correction is a research question here, not a product: it has held only in narrow, stated cases. Nothing we have published is peer-reviewed yet.
seeking: We welcome questions, replication attempts and test proposals from MLIP builders, benchmark maintainers, materials scientists and labs.
contactLine: Research partners, model builders, press and investors
knowsAbout: Benchmarking foundation models for atomistic simulation
Elastic and surface properties of metals

approach.text: Compare MLIP predictions with published reference values and record where, and in which direction, they miss.

Write the pass/fail gate down before a test or a correction runs, and label any amendment made after results are seen. Correction is a research question here, not a product: it has held only in narrow, stated cases. In four preregistered campaigns in July 2026 (Round 4), no gate passed: three failed and one abstained.

Release the data, the gate and the verdict together: pass, fail or abstain. Lean 4 checks the arithmetic and stated inequalities behind published numbers; it does not check the physics, the reference data or the pipeline.

tested.what: Blind prediction of fcc (110) surface-energy error
tested.scope: Nine fcc metals, four foundation MLIPs: an error field fitted to three other observables predicted the never-fitted (110) error at r = 0.906 across 36 model–material cells (material-clustered 95% CI 0.82–0.96; permutation null centred near 0.44; significant for three of the four models).
Blind (110) surface-energy error fell from 9.7% to 1.5% on nickel and from 28.0% to 13.7% on copper: one model, two metals, one facet.
Across 21 materials and 228 published reference values, four foundation MLIPs ranked surface energies almost correctly (Spearman 0.88–1.00) while missing magnitudes by tens of percent.

tested.what: Shared error direction across models (21-material benchmark)
tested.scope: Apparent cross-model alignment sat inside a coupling-aware null, so we do not count it as a result.

Four MatPES MLIPs, 128 cases, r2SCAN targets approximate: one bias direction per functional transfers out of sample. When the held-out reference sets how far to correct, MAE falls from 17.84 to 10.36 GPa: a ceiling, not a deployable correction. A correction that works without seeing the answer is still open, and derived moduli are uncertified.
On the same 16-metal panel, 1×1×1 TensorNet/PBE cells matched 3×3×3 cells for elastic-constant error (14.55 vs 14.61 GPa MAE).

tested.what: Global elastic correction on that panel
tested.scope: A global correction made the result worse: 63.40 GPa MAE.
30-path panel; MACE-MP-0 small and medium, MACE-MPA-0 medium and CHGNet missed a 40 meV gate (MAE 135.0–242.5 meV on completed paths).
Rocksalt ionics and perovskites: ionics 0/4; perovskites 0/1 after a post-measurement amendment.
Every selected Δ-correction made holdout error worse.
Four of seven registered predictions across two experiments failed and are reported as failures.
No available model had the spin physics the test needed.
On the 30-path Li-ion panel, fitted on 12 disjoint training paths: all four models abstained at the direction gate, so no correction was applied.

The preregistered 40 meV gate against published VASP barriers failed on path 7 (118.8 meV). An amendment written after that failure moved the gate to a same-engine check, which passed; against the published references the error was 693.0–705.7 meV. Same-engine only.

can.text: For nine fcc metals, an error field fitted to three other observables predicted the never-fitted (110) surface-energy error of four foundation MLIPs at r = 0.906 across 36 model–material cells (material-clustered 95% CI 0.82–0.96; permutation null centred near 0.44; significant for three of the four models).
Used as an energy-only correction beside CHGNet, the field cut blind (110) surface-energy error from 9.7% to 1.5% on nickel and from 28.0% to 13.7% on copper: one model, two metals, one facet.
Across 21 materials and 228 published reference values, four foundation MLIPs ranked surface energies almost correctly (Spearman 0.88–1.00) while missing magnitudes by tens of percent.
On 16 elemental cubic metals, 1×1×1 TensorNet/PBE cells matched 3×3×3 cells for elastic-constant error (14.55 vs 14.61 GPa MAE).

cannot.text: That any correction we have tested is ready to deploy. In four preregistered campaigns in July 2026 (Round 4), no gate passed: three failed and one abstained. On the 16-metal elastic panel, 17.84 → 10.36 GPa is a ceiling that needs the held-out answer, not a deployable correction.
That different models share one error direction on surface energies. In our 21-material benchmark, apparent cross-model alignment sat inside a coupling-aware null.
That a Lean check confirms the physics. Lean 4 checks the arithmetic and stated inequalities behind published numbers; it does not check the physics, the reference data or the pipeline.
Anything about the newest multi-head or multi-fidelity models or their confidence heads. We have not tested them.
Peer review. No Lupine paper has been peer-reviewed or accepted yet.

operatingModel.summary: Lupine Science is founder-led (Alex Welcing, founder). The work is done with AI coding and research agents under rules that live in code. AI assistance is disclosed, and a human author is responsible for every public summary.
rules: In the research workbench, a pull request that changes a status in the assumption registry, the status-event snapshot or the locked ontology must bring a new evidence-bundle hash, or CI fails. The check does not read claim files, the Markdown ledgers or article status lines; those are reviewed by hand.
Public research-activity records pass a reviewed import that rejects local paths, emails, private URLs and credential-shaped strings; failed or stopped work cannot be relabelled completed.

The model review stage runs with an explicit tool list: packet critiques run without tools, and literature jobs can search and fetch public web pages. It cannot start experiments, publish or schedule runs.
A model's score is a recommendation, not evidence.
Lean must build with no sorry, and theorem counts are generated, never typed.

Partner-facing evaluation is designed to run in an offline HPC lane on the partner's own hardware: local manifests in, local JSON out, no outbound connections at runtime, telemetry off by default. That container has not yet been built on a facility cluster.
operatingModel.dataFlow: Agent model calls go to commercial model providers, through API keys and the providers' own signed-in command-line tools. Agent traces go to an Arize Phoenix tracing project. Benchmark runs use Lupine's cloud project or a local workstation.
operatingModel.keyPerson: Key-person risk is real: the program depends on one founder. Public data, code and the failure ledger mean the results can be checked without us.
